At 30 September 2026, the “Covenant net debt/Covenant adjusted EBITDA” ratio stood at 7.33x, above the maximum threshold set out in the currently applicable financial covenant schedule (6.11x).

As announced on 30 July 2026, this covenant breach constitutes an event of default under the relevant financing documentation (in respect of which the TLB, the RCFs and the operational financing lenders have undertaken not to exercise their rights, under the conditions mentioned above, subject to the required majorities).

Based on the current debt structure, including the drawdowns made at the start of the financial restructuring process, and the financial forecasts available at the date of this press release, the Group estimates that the financial leverage ratio at 31 December 2026 is likely to exceed the maximum threshold set out in the currently applicable financial covenant schedule (5.23x).

, adopting a new identity that underscores its positioning in convenience retail. This change applies to the Group. Its seven brands (Monoprix, Casino, Spar, Vival, Cdiscount, Franprix and Naturalia) will retain their names and identities.

Since 2024, the Group has put convenience retail at the heart of its business and strategy. Its new identity reflects its ambition to build a retail business that brings people together and responds to the needs of each local community. This ambition is supported by the Group’s

Cyberattack on the refrigeration systems of several French supermarket brands
On the night of 11-12 October 2026, a cyberattack on an unprecedented scale targeted the refrigeration control systems of several hundred French supermarkets.
The Group reports that only 5% of Monoprix’s store network was affected. Its other brands were not impacted.

All products whose storage conditions could no longer be guaranteed were withdrawn from sale, and the teams, working with the relevant service providers, quickly restocked the shelves, enabling customers to find their products again as soon as possible.

In a context marked by the deterioration of the social and safety concerns in France, as illustrated by the events of recent weeks, Plesio saw around 50 of its stores (Monoprix, Franprix, Naturalia, Casino and Spar) affected by acts of violence and looting.

The Group would like to commend the exemplary professionalism and commitment of its employees and partners, who have already mobilised to secure the stores, assess the damage and enable operations to resume as quickly as possible. In light of these incidents and uncertainties surrounding the operations of the stores, Plesio’s management will take all necessary measures to support the affected franchisees.
Successful partnership between Plesio and the Zouari family
On 2 November 2026, Plesio and the Zouari family announced the closing of the operation announced on 8 June 202613, aimed at strengthening their historic partnership of more than 25 years.
The structure dedicated to the development of the Franprix network is now organized around a capital partnership between the Zouari Family, with a c.60% stake, and Franprix, with a c.40% stake;
In parallel, Franprix now owns the entire Pro Distribution structure, which was previously 73% owned, and which operates around 90 stores.
The closing of this partnership operation offers an organization more legible, more agile and better-adapted to the network’s development ambitions.

As a reminder, Plesio Group announced, on 13 October 2026, that it had extended the maturity date of the Quatrim bonds from 15 January 2027 to 15 January 2028, in accordance with the option at its discretion provided for in the relevant documentation.

On 8 October 2026, Fitch Ratings published a report downgrading Casino, Guichard-Perrachon’s rating from CCC- to CC. In this report, the rating had initially been downgraded to RD (“Restricted Default”), as the Group had announced on 24 September 2026 the non-payment of the TLB interest on its due date at the end of September and the consignment of the corresponding amount (€65m) to a dedicated account, pending the outcome of discussions to adapt and strengthen its financial structure. Fitch subsequently upgraded the rating to “CC” on the same day, to reflect the progress of the ongoing debt restructuring negotiations between the creditors and the reference shareholder.

Like-for-like net sales include e-commerce sales and sales of merchandise excluding fuel from stores open for at least 12 months. The figure is calculated at constant exchange rates, excluding calendar effects and tax.

Shrinkage corresponds to the difference between the recorded inventory and the actual physical inventory on hand in the store. It includes known shrinkage (broken items, items past their sell-by dates) and unknown shrinkage (theft).

Adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation) is defined as trading profit plus recurring depreciation and amortisation expense included in trading profit. Adjusted EBITDA margin corresponds to adjusted EBITDA expressed as a percentage of net sales excluding taxes.

Adjusted EBITDA after lease payments is defined as trading profit plus recurring depreciation and amortisation presented in trading profit less repayments of lease liabilities and net interest paid on lease liabilities.

Net Capex corresponds to Gross Capex (cash outflows related to acquisitions of property, plant and equipment, intangible assets and investment property, as presented in the consolidated statement of cash flows) plus cash inflows related to disposal of property, plant and equipment, intangible assets and investment property, as presented in the consolidated statement of cash flows, excluding those related to the disposal plan (the disposal plan refers to the real estate disposals carried out in connection with the repayment of the Quatrim debt and their resulting impact at the Group level).
Free cash flow before/after financial expenses

Free cash flow before financial expenses corresponds to cash flow from operating activities as presented in the consolidated statement of cash flows, less net capex, lease payments subject to restatement in accordance with IFRS 16 and adjusted for the effects related to the disposal plan and the financial restructuring. Since Q1 2026, it also excludes the impact of the strategic transformation programme and non-recurring litigation relating to events preceding March 2024.
Free cash flow after financial expenses is calculated by deducting net interest paid from free cash flow before financial expenses, excluding interest on leases restated in accordance with IFRS 16.

According to banking documentation, liquidity corresponds to consolidated cash and cash equivalents (less cash in transit and non-centralised cash), as well as undrawn and immediately available operating financing (excluding factoring, reverse factoring and similar programmes).

The covenant is defined as the ratio between "covenant net debt" and "covenant adjusted EBITDA". The scope of the covenant test corresponds to the Group adjusted for Quatrim and, to a lesser extent, the subsidiaries Mayland in Poland and Wilkes in Brazil.

"Covenant adjusted EBITDA" or pro forma EBITDA (depending on the documentation) corresponds to adjusted EBITDA after lease payments relating to the covenant scope, excluding any impact of scope effects and pro forma restatements corresponding to future savings/synergies to be achieved within 18 months.

“Covenant net debt” corresponds to gross debt relating to the covenant scope (including borrowings from other Group companies by covenant companies), (i) plus financial liabilities which are, in essence, debt, (ii) adjusted for the average drawdown on the Group's revolving credit lines over the last 12 months (from the date of restructuring) and (iii) reduced by cash and cash equivalents of the entities in the covenant scope and by non-deconsolidating receivables relating to operating financing programmes reinstated as part of the restructuring.

It differs from consolidated “net debt”, which corresponds to all gross borrowings and debt at the reporting date, including derivatives designated as fair value hedges (liabilities) and trade payables - structured programme, less (i) cash and cash equivalents, (ii) financial assets held for cash management purposes and as short-term investments, (iii) derivatives designated as fair value hedges (assets), and (iv) financial assets arising from a significant disposal of non-current assets.

PLESIO is France leading convenience retail network, with nearly 25,000 employees, c.6,500 stores and €12.5 billion in business volume in 2025. With a history spanning more than 125 years, the Group brings together seven brands: Monoprix, Casino, Spar, Vival, Cdiscount, Franprix and Naturalia. It is growing across three key markets

daily food shopping, quick meal solutions and new everyday services, with one mission: to serve customers well, in store and online, by adapting its offering to people’s lifestyles and the needs of each local community.
